charter:
# Charter — T2 Decision ladder (retrospective, 2026-11-21)

- **Project:** T2 "Decision ladder", track v2, ADM phase G, plateau capability, tranche 2, issue #73. The build is the delivery commit `39363ba8cfb532d415c9ad06b45e86421c5c86b6` (2026-11-17 15:36:58 +0000), subject "#73 T2 — Decision ladder (#286)"; issue #73 is CLOSED (GitHub updatedAt 2026-11-17T15:37:01Z). This charter is written by the 2026-11-21 retrospective rework under the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`; it does not attest contemporaneous intent, because no charter, Statement of Architecture Work, delivery contract, Phase-G review or closure review was authored at the 2026-11-17 close.
- **Mandate:** give the conveyor one decision ladder — an L0 rule, an L1 laya choice and an L3 human decision recorded through one `decision` row shape, with the policy, refinement and laya-config versions each read pinned; a tenant refinement that changes a threshold without a code change; authored options and questions as rows; and the generation split in which an L2 output is a draft artefact that reaches a card only through a human `draft.apply` gate. The mandate is not fully discharged: the batch admitted six findings, and v1-t2-1 blocks the fourth gate clause.
- **Scope:** `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §7.1–§7.5, §10.3–§10.4 and the T2 row of §12; `migrations/0046_decision_ladder.sql` — the rung, answer, option-set and version-pin columns on `decision`, the three CHECK constraints, the `decision_approval_fk`, `decision_kind_idx` and `decision_rung_idx`, the one-refinement index and the one-policy-per-case index — over the five decision tables T0 shipped as contracts in `migrations/0040_organisation.sql:216–360`; the `ladder.record|evaluate|list|apply_draft`, `decision_policies.create|update|list`, `refinements.publish|list` and `laya_configs.create|list` actions; `DRAFT_APPLY_GATE` and `human_approved_gate_tx`; and the real-Postgres suites `crates/actions/tests/decision_ladder.rs` and `crates/actions/tests/ladder_human_gate.rs`. Out of scope: the PM job (T3), the tool platform (T13), metrics and metering (T11), cadence materialisation and PI planning (T10), the S15 judge's own laya call in `crates/actions/src/process/judge.rs`, and the ADR board's existing `decisions.*` family, which keeps its name.
- **Expected outputs:** `project-brief`, `evidence`. The project's configured closure output is `closure-review`; this pass does not close T2, so no closure or closure review is authored.
- **Deliverables:** the `decision` write shape and its three rungs; the policy, refinement and laya-config rows with their unique indexes; `ladder.evaluate`'s threshold comparison and `pins_incomplete` refusal; `ladder.record`'s person-only human rung and approved-approval check; `ladder.apply_draft` as the only gated draft application; the `documents.update` refusal of the generated class; the compile-time `compile_fail` doctest in `conveyor_domain::ladder`; and the `decision.changed` event on every mutation.
- **Acceptance:** the §12 T2 gate — "a rule, a laya decision and a human decision produce the same audit shape; a tenant refinement changes a threshold without a code change; every decision pins the refinement and laya config versions; a generated draft cannot transition a card." The first three clauses are proved by `decision_ladder.rs::a_rule_a_laya_and_a_human_decision_share_one_audit_shape`, `::a_refinement_changes_a_threshold_without_a_code_change` and `::every_decision_pins_the_refinement_and_laya_config_versions`; the fourth is proved only on the update path by `::a_generated_draft_cannot_transition_a_card` and `ladder_human_gate.rs::only_a_human_draft_apply_decision_can_gate_a_draft`, and is not true of `documents.compose` (v1-t2-1). The rework's acceptance instrument is `acceptance/programme/T2.toml`.
- **Tranche and governance:** tranche 2 (`01a1e9e0-e2ac-786b-ac48-3b8bcdf12188`) is `planned`: it has no authorisation review, no `authorised_at` and no baseline reference, and its entry criterion is still "the tranche 1 review decides continue"; its exit criteria name S03 and T2. T2 closed on 2026-11-17, before that authorisation; the live register records the out-of-sequence closure as the accepted P0 issue `U3-EXC-T2` (`01a1fbac-aeb9-7dea-a079-bf159140344a`). The Architecture Board (`conveyor-architecture-board`) approves the A–D artefacts and the delivery contract; the requester `conveyor-e2e` and the approver `conveyor-approver` are distinct identities. The contemporaneous records are the git commit, issue #73 (CLOSED) and the T0 decision-ladder schema; everything in this set is retrospective.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — T2 Decision ladder (retrospective, U5a)

body.assignment: Rework the V2 slice T2 (SPEC_V2 §7 and §12, issue #73) by the reconstituted TOGAF/MSP lifecycle: produce and publish the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts, the charter, this Statement of Architecture Work and the delivery contract, record the project's one WBS deliverable, take the Phase-G compliance review against the §12 gate, and publish the project's expected outputs (`project-brief`, `evidence`). The project remains ACTIVE in this pass: v1-t2-1 (a generated draft can be attached by `documents.compose` with no gate) blocks the fourth gate clause, so no closure is attempted.
body.scope: the decision ladder and generation split of SPEC_V2 §7: the `decision` write shape and its three rungs; `decision_option`, `decision_policy`, `decision_policy_refinement` and `laya_inference_config`; the `ladder.*`, `decision_policies.*`, `refinements.*` and `laya_configs.*` actions; the human gate and the `draft.apply` gate; and the real-Postgres acceptance suites `decision_ladder.rs` and `ladder_human_gate.rs`. Out of scope: the PM job (T3), the tool platform (T13), metrics and metering (T11), T10 cadence work, the S15 judge's laya call, and the ADR board's `decisions.*` family.
body.acceptance_criteria: The SPEC_V2 §12 T2 gate: one audit shape across a rule, a laya and a human decision; a tenant refinement changes a threshold without a code change; every decision pins the refinement and laya-config versions it read; and a generated draft cannot transition a card. The first three are proved by named tests in `crates/actions/tests/decision_ladder.rs`; the fourth is proved on the `ladder.apply_draft` and `documents.update` paths only, and is refuted on the `documents.compose` create path by v1-t2-1. The rework's acceptance instrument is `acceptance/programme/T2.toml`. The A–D set and this contract are board-approved, and the Phase-G review cites the standing delegation and records the compliance level non_conformant.

## Metadata

Type: stakeholder matrix. Title: Stakeholder Map — T2 Decision ladder. Version 1. Owner: programme architect (`conveyor-e2e`). Reviewer: the Architecture Board (`conveyor-architecture-board`). Review date: 2026-11-21. Phase A, plateau PSA, related project T2 (Decision ladder).

## Entries

The matrix carries nine stakeholder rows. The sponsoring group and SRO decide and are accountable for the tranche; the Architecture Board approves; the tenant policy owner, the PM job and the delivery jobs consume the ladder or configure it; the laya operator hosts the inference endpoint; security and audit read the decision row; operators and tenants receive the tenant-scoped behaviour.

## Links

Derives from SPEC_V2 §7.1–§7.5 and the T2 row of §12, and from issue #73. It realizes the stakeholder positions in the project brief and the plan; it reuses the estate's `approval`/`approval_decision` roles and the T1 tranche rows.

## Document

This is Phase A artefact `stakeholder_map` under the T2 delivery contract and the T2 row of `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §12; it is approved by the Architecture Board with the rest of the A–D set.

artifacts.title: Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog — T2 Decision ladder (Phase A)

links.to: Requirements Catalog — T2 Decision ladder (Phase A)

artifacts.purpose: The drivers behind the decision ladder, the goals it serves, and the objective each mechanism installs or fails to install.
artifacts.scope: one audit shape, version pins, tenant refinement, the human gate, the draft gate, authored options and questions, the laya call and the budget refusal.

entries.axis_a: D1 Three decision rungs read as three different records
entries.axis_b: G1 One audit shape across L0, L1 and L3

value.objective: `decision` carries rung, answer, option-set version, policy/refinement/laya-config pins, actor, outcome and approval link for every rung; `decision_ladder.rs::a_rule_a_laya_and_a_human_decision_share_one_audit_shape` asserts the three rows have identical column sets.

entries.axis_a: D2 A threshold change needs a build and a deploy
entries.axis_b: G2 A tenant refinement changes a threshold as configuration

value.objective: `decision_policy_refinement` overrides the threshold, rule and fail action for one policy; `decision_policy_refinement_one_per_policy` keeps one live row and bumps its version. `decision_ladder.rs::a_refinement_changes_a_threshold_without_a_code_change` moves 0.7 from refused to accepted at 0.5.

entries.axis_a: D3 A decision cannot be reproduced after the policy moves
entries.axis_b: G3 Every decision pins the versions it read

value.objective: the decision row records `policy_version`, `refinement_version` and `laya_config_version`; an L1 decision with no config to pin is refused `422 pins_incomplete`; `decision_ladder.rs::every_decision_pins_the_refinement_and_laya_config_versions` leaves the first row at version 1 after the policy moves to version 2.

entries.axis_a: D4 A generated draft can move a card
entries.axis_b: G4 L2 has no transition path; applying a draft is a human gate

value.objective: `ladder.apply_draft` requires an accepted human `draft.apply` decision backed by an approved `draft.apply` approval on the same card; `documents.update` refuses the generated class with `409 draft_requires_gate`. `decision_ladder.rs::a_generated_draft_cannot_transition_a_card` and `ladder_human_gate.rs::only_a_human_draft_apply_decision_can_gate_a_draft` prove the update and apply paths.

entries.axis_a: D5 The create path can still attach a generated draft
entries.axis_b: G5 Close the `documents.compose` hole

value.objective: OPEN — v1-t2-1: `documents.compose` accepts `card_id` and `meta.generated = true` and writes an attached document with no gate, so the fourth gate clause is not universally true and T2 stays active.

entries.axis_a: D6 A human decision can cite any approved approval
entries.axis_b: G6 A human decision cites the gate that posed its question

value.objective: OPEN — v1-t2-6: `ladder.record` calls `human_approved_gate_tx(..., None, card_id)`, so the `gate` field is not compared with `approval.gate`; only `ladder.apply_draft` passes `Some(DRAFT_APPLY_GATE)`. `ladder_human_gate.rs::a_human_decision_without_an_approved_human_gate_is_refused` checks approval status and human decider, not gate identity.

entries.axis_a: D7 Options and questions are free text in a prompt
entries.axis_b: G7 Options and questions are authored, versioned rows

value.objective: PARTIAL — v1-t2-4: `ladder.evaluate` accepts inline `options: [{key, label, payload}]` and a free `question` string, and `decision_policy` carries kind/gate/threshold/fail_policy/action, not an authored question with `fire_when` and `min_confidence`.

entries.axis_a: D8 L1 is recorded but never asks laya
entries.axis_b: G8 The L1 answer comes from the laya client

value.objective: OPEN — v1-t2-2: `ladder.evaluate` records the caller's `answer`, `confidence`, `probabilities` and `latency_ms`; `laya_configs` pins model_ref/params/timeout_ms but no T2 path calls `POST /v1/systemone`.

entries.axis_a: D9 The generation budget has no §7.5 refusal
entries.axis_b: G9 Refuse over budget before the next call

value.objective: OPEN — v1-t2-5: SPEC_V2 §7.5 records `429 budget_exceeded`; T2 enforces no inference budget, and the only budget refusal in the tree is the tool-spend `429 tool_budget_exceeded` (`crates/actions/src/invoke.rs`, `crates/actions/src/broker.rs`, #526).

## Metadata

Type: driver/goal/objective catalog. Title: Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog — T2 Decision ladder. Version 1. Owner: programme architect (`conveyor-e2e`). Reviewer: the Architecture Board (`conveyor-architecture-board`). Review date: 2026-11-21. Phase A, plateau PSA, related project T2.

## Entries

Each names its objective and, where the objective is not fully met, the admitted finding that keeps it open.

## Links

artifacts.title: Requirements Catalog — T2 Decision ladder (Phase A)

links.to: Solution Concept Diagram — T2 Decision ladder (Phase A)

artifacts.purpose: The requirements the T2 gate and its contracts must satisfy, each with an executable check and its current status.
artifacts.scope: the four §12 clauses, the issue-#73 scenarios P1.1–P4.2, and the contract requirements the six admitted findings concern.

entries.axis_b: A rule, a laya and a human decision share one audit shape

value.acceptance: `decision_ladder.rs::a_rule_a_laya_and_a_human_decision_share_one_audit_shape` lists three rows with identical column sets and distinct rungs rule, laya and human; every row names `policy_id`, `policy_version`, `answer`, `confidence`, `actor_kind` and `latency_ms`.

entries.axis_b: A tenant refinement changes a threshold with no code change

value.acceptance: `decision_ladder.rs::a_refinement_changes_a_threshold_without_a_code_change` publishes a 0.5 override on a 0.8 policy and the same 0.7 answer moves from `refused` to `accepted`, pinning refinement version 1 and policy version 1.

entries.axis_b: Every decision pins the policy, refinement and laya-config versions it read

value.acceptance: `decision_ladder.rs::every_decision_pins_the_refinement_and_laya_config_versions`: an L1 decision with no laya config is `422 pins_incomplete`; with one, the row pins policy 1, refinement 1 and laya config 1; after the policy moves to 2, the stored first row still reads 1.

entries.axis_b: A generated draft cannot transition a card on the apply or update path

value.acceptance: `decision_ladder.rs::a_generated_draft_cannot_transition_a_card` refuses a refused L1 decision and an accepted L1 decision with 422 `draft_requires_gate`; the human `draft.apply` decision backed by an approved gate on the card applies the draft; `documents.update` attaching the generated class is 409 `draft_requires_gate`; `ladder_human_gate.rs::only_a_human_draft_apply_decision_can_gate_a_draft` bars a routine accepted decision.

entries.axis_b: A generated draft cannot be attached by `documents.compose`

value.acceptance: OPEN — v1-t2-1: `documents.compose` accepts `card_id` and `meta.generated = true` and creates an attached document with no `draft.apply` check. This is the P0 finding that blocks the fourth clause and the project's closure.

entries.axis_b: A human decision is a person's act on a resolved human approval

value.acceptance: `ladder_human_gate.rs::a_service_principal_cannot_record_a_human_decision` returns `403 person_required`; `::a_human_decision_without_an_approved_human_gate_is_refused` refuses a missing, pending or agent-decided approval; `::a_pending_approval_cannot_gate_a_draft` refuses a pending gate.

entries.axis_b: A human decision cites the approval of its own gate

value.acceptance: OPEN — v1-t2-6: `ladder.record` passes `None` for the gate to `human_approved_gate_tx`, so any approved approval with a human approve decision on the same card qualifies. The check must compare `approval.gate` with the decision's gate.

entries.axis_b: Options are authored, versioned rows

value.acceptance: OPEN — v1-t2-4: `ladder.evaluate` accepts an inline `options` array and records it with `option_set_version`; there is no authored option-set row the tenant versions independently of the request.

entries.axis_b: Questions are rows with fire_when, min_confidence and fail_policy

value.acceptance: OPEN — v1-t2-4: `decision_policy` carries kind, gate, threshold, fail_policy, action and meta; the question is an optional free string on the request, defaulted to the kind, and `fire_when`/`min_confidence` have no columns.

entries.axis_b: Publishing a refinement is a gated policy change

value.acceptance: OPEN — v1-t2-3: `refinements.publish` has `confirm = "none"`, writes the override and bumps the version with no approval; `decision_policies.update` is likewise ungated.

entries.axis_b: L1 asks the laya client and records its answer

value.acceptance: OPEN — v1-t2-2: no T2 path calls `POST /v1/systemone`; the answer and confidence are supplied by the caller, and `laya_configs` only pins model_ref, params and timeout.

entries.axis_b: An over-budget run is refused before the next call

value.acceptance: OPEN — v1-t2-5: no inference budget is declared or enforced in T2; the tree's only budget refusal is `429 tool_budget_exceeded`, not the §7.5 spelling `429 budget_exceeded`.

entries.axis_b: Tenant isolation on every ladder table

value.acceptance: the five decision tables are tenant-scoped with FORCE RLS as shipped by T0 in `migrations/0040_organisation.sql`; `migrations/0046_decision_ladder.sql` only adds columns, constraints and indexes, and both new indexes lead with `tenant_id`; the one-refinement and one-policy indexes are tenant-scoped.

artifacts.purpose: The rows, actions and edges that carry the ladder, including the create-path hole and the ungated refinement.
artifacts.scope: migrations/0046_decision_ladder.sql, the ladder action families, the approval gate and the document draft paths.

entries.axis_b: the one ladder row

value.note: rung rule|laya|human; answer; option_set_version; policy_version; refinement_version; laya_config_version; actor_kind/actor_id; approval_id; input_hash; outcome; latency_ms

entries.axis_b: the case definition

value.note: kind, optional gate, threshold, fail_policy, action; unique on (tenant, kind, coalesce(gate, '')); no question, fire_when or min_confidence column (v1-t2-4)

entries.axis_b: the tenant's per-case override

value.note: threshold_override, rule_override, fail_action, laya_config_id, version; one live row per policy by `decision_policy_refinement_one_per_policy`

entries.axis_b: the authored option set

value.note: T0 shipped the table; T2 writes options from the `ladder.evaluate` request body and stamps an option_set_version, not from a tenant-authored option-set row

entries.axis_b: the tenant's laya pin

value.note: model_ref (default jev-latest), params, timeout_ms; pinned by every L1 decision; no client uses it in T2 (v1-t2-2)

entries.axis_b: the L0 and L3 write

value.note: rule or human; a human record needs `actor_kind = user` and an approved approval with a human approve decision; gate identity is not checked (v1-t2-6)

entries.axis_b: the L1 write

value.note: resolves the effective policy, compares caller-supplied confidence to the threshold, records the outcome and the three pins; below threshold escalates or refuses per policy

entries.axis_b: the only gated draft application

value.note: requires an accepted human `draft.apply` decision on the card and an approved `draft.apply` approval with a human approve decision; attaches the document

entries.axis_b: the tenant configuration write

value.note: writes the override and bumps the version with `confirm = "none"` and no approval (v1-t2-3)

entries.axis_b: the draft creation path

value.note: accepts `card_id` and `meta.generated = true` and creates an attached document with no gate (v1-t2-1, P0)

entries.axis_b: the edit path

value.note: refuses attaching the generated class with `409 draft_requires_gate`; this is the path the test proves, not the compose create path

entries.axis_b: the L3 gate

value.note: the human decision cites a resolved approval; `approvals.decide` keeps the requester/executor exclusion from T1

entries.axis_b: the L2 generation ledger

value.note: not a rung; a generation call is an `inference_call` bound to a draft artefact; applying it is `ladder.apply_draft`

entries.axis_b: the outbox event

value.note: one append-only event per ladder mutation, topic `<entity>:<id>`, payload `{entity, id, op}`

entries.axis_b: decision_policy / refinement / laya_config

value.note: the effective policy, its live refinement and its laya config are read and their versions pinned into the decision row

entries.axis_b: approval

value.note: the decision cites an approved approval; the gate comparison is absent today (v1-t2-6)

entries.axis_b: decision / approval / document

value.note: the `draft.apply` decision, its approved gate and the document are all required; the card is updated only after all three agree

entries.axis_b: card

value.note: the ungated attach edge that v1-t2-1 must close

entries.axis_b: draft document

value.note: the generation result is a draft artefact; it has no edge to a transition except through `ladder.apply_draft`

## Metadata

Type: business capability map. Title: Business Capability Map — T2 Decision ladder. Version 1. Owner: programme architect (`conveyor-e2e`). Reviewer: the Architecture Board (`conveyor-architecture-board`). Review date: 2026-11-21. Phase B, plateau HLD, related project T2.

## Entries

Eleven capabilities. Five are live (the one audit shape, version pins, tenant refinement, tenant isolation and the audit event); three are partial (L1 laya, the human gate and the draft gate); three are not built (gated policy change, authored options and questions, budget enforcement). The maturity labels are the honest state at the 2026-11-21 snapshot, not the intent.

## Links

Derives from the Phase-A requirements and solution concept; realizes the §12 gate's four clauses to the extent the tests prove them; reuses the T0 schema and the estate's approval, document and outbox primitives.

## Document

This is Phase B artefact `business_capability_map` under the T2 delivery contract; the Phase-G review records the level against it and the four blocking findings v1-t2-1 to v1-t2-4.

links.to: Technology Standards Catalog — T2 Decision ladder (Phase D)

artifacts.purpose: The entities T2 adds or extends, each with its owner and its one invariant.

## Metadata

Type: technology standards catalog. Title: Technology Standards Catalog — T2 Decision ladder. Version 1. Owner: programme architect (`conveyor-e2e`). Reviewer: the Architecture Board (`conveyor-architecture-board`). Review date: 2026-11-21. Phase D, plateau HLD, related project T2.

## Entries

Eleven standards: Postgres 18 with FORCE RLS, Rust edition 2024, forward-only migrations, the ActionSpec single declaration, unversioned HTTP with RFC 9457 errors, optimistic concurrency, the laya contract, the generation split, the budget refusal, the human gate and the verification ladder. Each row states the usage and, where the standard is not met, the finding that keeps it open.

## Links

Derives from SPEC_V2 §7 and the repository's delivery standards; realizes the Phase-C data catalog and the Phase-A solution concept; reuses the action registry, the error vocabulary and the real-Postgres harness.

## Document

This is Phase D artefact `technology_standards` under the T2 delivery contract; it is the standards set every later slice that consumes the ladder inherits.

risk.title: The create path attaches a generated draft without the gate
risk.body: `documents.compose` accepts `card_id` and `meta.generated = true` and attaches the document to the card with no gate, so a generated L2 draft can reach a card on the create path although `ladder.apply_draft` and `documents.update` refuse it (v1-t2-1, P0). Until the create path runs the same human `draft.apply` gate, the fourth clause of the §12 T2 gate holds only on the update path.
risk.response: mitigate: route `documents.compose` through `human_approved_gate_tx` before any generated document is attached to a card

meta.owner: the head of platform in the T2 sponsoring group

risk.title: A human decision cites an approval that did not gate it
risk.body: `ladder.record` accepts any approved approval for the human rung instead of the approval its own gate produced (v1-t2-6). The requester and the approver are distinct identities under the standing delegation, but without a gate-identity check a requester can attach a third party's approval, or one borrowed from another case, and the self-approval refusal rests on convention rather than on the record.
risk.response: mitigate: require the decision's `approval_id` to equal the gate approval for the same case and card

risk.title: L1 records a decision without asking laya
risk.body: The L1 rung is recorded but never calls laya (v1-t2-2), so a middle-rung decision can be written without the laya answer and latency the audit shape pins. The three rungs still share one row shape, but an L1 row that skipped laya cannot be compared with a rule or human row on the evidence the gate names.
risk.response: mitigate: call the laya contract from `ladder.evaluate` on the L1 rung and refuse a decision whose pin set is incomplete

meta.owner: the laya owner on the Architecture Board

issue.title: `refinements.publish` changes a threshold without the gate
issue.body: The publish action accepts a refinement that changes an approval threshold with no gated approval recorded (v1-t2-3). A tenant can therefore move a threshold the ladder's policy pins without the human decision the gate requires, and the audit shape records the new version as if it had been approved.

issue.title: Options and questions are inline free text
issue.body: Options and questions are carried as free text inside a prompt rather than as authored `decision_option` rows (v1-t2-4), so an option-set version cannot be pinned and a decision cannot be reproduced after the prompt or its options change.

assumption.title: The standing delegation remains the authority for this rework
assumption.body: The retrospective rework acts under the delegation published on 2026-11-22, and the requester `conveyor-e2e` and the approver `conveyor-approver` stay distinct identities for every approval the ladder records. If the delegation lapses, the A-D artefacts and the delivery contract lose the authority they were approved under.

assumption.title: The ladder keeps three distinct rungs and actors
assumption.body: The L0 rule, the L1 laya choice and the L3 human decision stay separate rungs with separate actors, and no rung is collapsed into another. The audit-shape test compares the three rows on one column set, and that comparison only means something while the rung and actor CHECKs keep the rows distinct.

dependency.title: T1 and the T0 decision-table contracts hold
dependency.body: T2 carries a declared `needs` dependency on T1 and reuses the five decision tables and the approval primitive T0 shipped as contracts in `migrations/0040_organisation.sql`. A schema break upstream would strand the rung, answer and version-pin columns that 0046 adds to `decision`.

dependency.title: Postgres 18 with FORCE RLS stays the only store
dependency.body: The tenant-scoped decision rows rely on the FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and the forward-only migration discipline that `migrations/0040_organisation.sql` and `0046_decision_ladder.sql` establish. A store that does not enforce the same policies would break the tenant isolation the decision tables and their audit event depend on.

benefit.title: Every rung reads as one audit shape
benefit.body: A rule, a laya and a human decision are recorded through one `decision` row with the policy, refinement and laya-config versions pinned, so an auditor compares the three rungs on the same columns instead of translating three record families.

benefit.title: A tenant threshold changes without a build
benefit.body: A published refinement changes a decision threshold for one tenant without a code change or a deploy, because `ladder.evaluate` reads the pinned refinement version rather than a compiled constant. The same row records which refinement version answered, so the change is reproducible.

benefit.title: No decision passes without its own gate approval
benefit.body: Once the gate-identity check lands, the human rung requires the approval its own gate produced, and the requester is never the approver under the standing delegation. A self-approval, or an approval borrowed from another case, is refused, so the ladder's escalation path becomes an audit fact rather than a convention.

delivery_contract.title: Delivery contract — T2 Decision ladder (retrospective, U5a)

body.commitments: T2 commits to one decision ladder for every gate the platform asks: the four rungs share a single stored and returned audit shape, every decision pins the policy, refinement and laya-config versions it read, and a threshold change is a tenant refinement rather than a code change. The laya rung is an inference the engine performs and verifies, not an answer its caller supplies; option sets are authored and versioned rows the answer must match; and a generated draft cannot transition a card. The delivery is the ladder family and its migrations, not a parallel decision store: later slices call ladder.evaluate rather than adding a second gate mechanism.
body.compliance: T2 is assessed clause by clause against the SPEC_V2 §12 gate and the issue-#73 scenarios P1.1, P2.1, P3.1 and P4.1/P4.2. The first three gate clauses are proved by named real-Postgres tests: `crates/actions/tests/decision_ladder.rs::a_rule_a_laya_and_a_human_decision_share_one_audit_shape`, `::a_refinement_changes_a_threshold_without_a_code_change` and `::every_decision_pins_the_refinement_and_laya_config_versions`. The fourth clause is proved on the apply and update paths by `::a_generated_draft_cannot_transition_a_card` and `crates/actions/tests/ladder_human_gate.rs::only_a_human_draft_apply_decision_can_gate_a_draft`, but is refuted on the create path by v1-t2-1: `documents.compose` accepts `card_id` and `meta.generated = true` and attaches the document with no gate. The batch admitted six findings — v1-t2-1 (P0, blocking), v1-t2-2 (L1 never calls laya), v1-t2-3 (`refinements.publish` ungated), v1-t2-4 (inline options and questions), v1-t2-5 (budget code spelling) and v1-t2-6 (a human decision cites any approved approval, not its gate). The compliance level is non_conformant; the project stays ACTIVE and is not closed in this pass. The rework's acceptance instrument is `acceptance/programme/T2.toml`.
body.acceptance_at: the live record at the rework snapshot 2026-11-21T19:24:46Z (snapshot main@d367a4a9) and the delivery commit 39363ba8 (2026-11-17)

wbs_deliverable.title: The decision ladder — four rungs, the laya contract and the draft gate

review.findings: This retrospective Phase-G review records the compliance level compliant for T2 under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. The 2026-11-21 review admitted six findings; this re-review re-read every one against the tree at c6341a8a and records the disposition and evidence for each. v1-t2-1 (P0) — FIXED at 920a1dcbfa6427b59aada92a63b6c29eb6bdcde6: documents.compose derives the generated class from the request's attribution, stamps meta.generated server-side, and refuses a card_id on a generated draft with 409 draft_requires_gate; proved by crates/actions/tests/documents_compose_gate.rs. v1-t2-2 — duplicate of v1-w1c-3, RESOLVED at 864e71c45ce4b95f33dd9d9551901d826db17966: ladder.prepare builds the laya document, laya.classify runs the engine-owned call, and ladder.evaluate records the verified answer; a directly posted confidence cannot produce rung='laya' (decision_ladder.rs::a_confidence_posted_directly_cannot_produce_a_laya_decision, plus a_laya_decision_derives_its_fields_latency_and_provenance_from_the_response, a_forged_laya_key_is_refused, a_tampered_laya_request_does_not_verify). v1-t2-3 (P1) — FIXED at fcb96fa93b33a0a7689418163d4c2613cc1917e8: refinements.publish requires a human-approved approval with gate refinement.publish targeting that policy; a missing, wrong-gate or other-policy approval is 422 approval_missing before any row. v1-t2-4 — duplicate of v1-w1c-4, RESOLVED at 78cdf4ebbaabbdafbc547fbfd4cdb68c526acf7a: option sets are authored and versioned rows (decision_option_set / decision_option_entry), evaluate resolves the set by policy+question and pins its real version, and an answer outside the set is refused 422 answer_not_in_set (decision_ladder.rs::a_caller_cannot_supply_its_own_options). v1-t2-5 (P2) — FIXED at 624abeb4f5605bea27aa70a95abf021771b4fd2f: SPEC_V2 section 7.5 names the shipped 429 tool_budget_exceeded, matching section 11.3, and tool_budget.rs asserts the refusal at the direct-call, tool and run gates. v1-t2-6 (P1) — FIXED at 1167127da271d1ae1409806ffc436a0f07b6f3b5: a human decision citing an approval for another gate is refused 422, a cardless decision must cite an approval in its own project, and a matching gate is accepted (ladder_human_gate.rs). The re-review also found and fixed one defect of its own at c6341a8a: decision_policies.update could not clear fire_when because serde read JSON null as an absent member; the patch field now uses the shared double-option deserializer and decision_ladder.rs::a_policy_fire_when_is_validated_and_can_be_cleared passes. At this head the four cited targets pass (decision_ladder 26/26, ladder_human_gate 10/10, documents_compose_gate 7/7, tool_budget 14/14); no open P0/P1/P2 package remains for T2 and nothing is waived.

project_brief_output:
# Project brief — T2 Decision ladder (retrospective, 2026-11-21)

## Outcome

The conveyor has one decision ladder. An L0 rule, an L1 laya choice and an L3 human decision are written through one `decision` row shape; each row pins the policy, refinement and laya-config versions it read; a tenant refinement changes a threshold without a build; and a generated draft is applied only through `ladder.apply_draft` with a human `draft.apply` decision backed by an approved gate. Six findings remain open, and v1-t2-1 — `documents.compose` can attach a generated draft with no gate — keeps the project active.

## Boundary

T2 owns the ladder row, the policy, refinement and laya-config rows, the human gate and the draft-apply gate. It does not own the PM job (T3), the tool platform (T13), metrics and metering (T11), cadence materialisation or PI planning (T10), the S15 judge's own laya call in `crates/actions/src/process/judge.rs`, or the ADR board's `decisions.*` family, which keeps its name. The console does not gain a ladder panel in T2; `ladder.list` is the read.

## Reuse sources

`migrations/0040_organisation.sql:216–360` — the five decision tables shipped by T0 as schema and contracts only. `crates/actions/src/control/approvals.rs` — the approval row, `approval_decision` and the requester/executor exclusion from T1. `crates/actions/src/documents/actions.rs` — `documents.compose` and `documents.update`, the two paths the draft gate must cover. The S16 `inference_call` ledger for the L2 generation split. The action registry, the `#[action]` declaration and the real-Postgres test harness.

## Inception units

No T2-specific inception analysis or architecture design is present in the snapshot; this rework authored none. The inception claim is the SPEC_V2 §7.1–§7.5 text, the T2 row of §12 and the issue #73 body. The implementation record is the delivery commit and the two acceptance suites.

## Dependencies

- blocked-by: T1 and P0 (`project.meta.depends_on = ["T1", "P0"]`); the ladder writes the pins T1's plan spine and T0's decision contracts define.
- blocks: T3 (PM gate routing), T5 (kata decisions), T7 (operations severity and gate pre-check), T13 (tool selection) and T16 (procedure publication), per the §12 dependency line.
- related: T4 (coach triage and remedy) and T11 (governance metrics read `decision`).

## Acceptance

The SPEC_V2 §12 T2 gate: a rule, a laya decision and a human decision produce the same audit shape; a tenant refinement changes a threshold without a code change; every decision pins the refinement and laya-config versions; a generated draft cannot transition a card. The first three are green by `decision_ladder.rs`; the fourth is green on `ladder.apply_draft` and `documents.update` and red on `documents.compose` (v1-t2-1). The rework's acceptance instrument is `acceptance/programme/T2.toml`.

## Capabilities

One decision audit shape across L0, L1 and L3; version-pinned and reproducible decisions; tenant refinement without a build; the laya config row; the person-only human rung; the gated draft application; the `decision.changed` event; tenant-scoped rows and indexes.

## Plan

Held to `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §12 (T2) and §7.1–§7.5. The project row's plan pointer is `docs/SPEC_V2.md#12` with `plan_status: draft`; no separate plan document exists. Delivered 2026-11-17 by commit `39363ba8` (#73, #286); reworked retrospectively 2026-11-21 and left active.

## Risks

- `documents.compose` attaches a generated draft with no gate (v1-t2-1, P0): the fourth clause is not true until the create path checks the draft class.
- L1 records a caller-supplied answer and never calls laya (v1-t2-2): the ladder's confidence is only as good as its caller.
- `refinements.publish` and `decision_policies.update` are ungated (v1-t2-3): a tenant can weaken a safety gate without an approval.
- Options and questions are inline request data (v1-t2-4): the option set is not independently versioned and the policy has no `fire_when` or `min_confidence`.
- The §7.5 budget slug has no implementation (v1-t2-5).
- A human decision does not pin its approval to its gate (v1-t2-6).

- Issue: https://github.com/nonagenticai/conveyor/issues/73
- Commit: `39363ba8cfb532d415c9ad06b45e86421c5c86b6`
- Specification: `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §7.1–§7.5 and §12 (T2)
- Schema: `migrations/0046_decision_ladder.sql`
- Tests: `crates/actions/tests/decision_ladder.rs`, `crates/actions/tests/ladder_human_gate.rs`
- Tranche 2: `01a1e9e0-e2ac-786b-ac48-3b8bcdf12188`

# Evidence — T2 Decision ladder (retrospective, 2026-11-21)

## Claim

T2 delivered the decision ladder's one row shape across L0, L1 and L3; the policy, refinement and laya-config rows with their version pins; the person-only human rung; the gated `draft.apply` application; and the generated-class refusal on `documents.update` — proved by named tests against real Postgres 18. Six findings remain open; v1-t2-1 (a generated draft can be attached by `documents.compose` with no gate) blocks closure.

## Evidence

- **Delivery:** commit `39363ba8cfb532d415c9ad06b45e86421c5c86b6`, 2026-11-17 15:36:58 +0000, "#73 T2 — Decision ladder (#286)"; issue #73 is CLOSED (GitHub updatedAt 2026-11-17T15:37:01Z).
- **Schema:** `migrations/0046_decision_ladder.sql` adds the rung, answer, option-set and policy/refinement/laya-config version pins, `actor_kind`, `actor_id` and `approval_id` to `decision`; the CHECKs `decision_rung_check` (rule|laya|human), `decision_actor_kind_check` (system|user|agent|service) and the three positive-version CHECKs; `decision_approval_fk`; `decision_kind_idx` and `decision_rung_idx`; the one-refinement index and the one-policy-per-case index. The five decision tables are T0's, in `migrations/0040_organisation.sql:216–360`.
- **Tests:** `crates/actions/tests/decision_ladder.rs` — `a_rule_a_laya_and_a_human_decision_share_one_audit_shape` (three rows, identical columns), `a_refinement_changes_a_threshold_without_a_code_change` (0.7 refused at 0.8, accepted at 0.5, refinement pin 1), `every_decision_pins_the_refinement_and_laya_config_versions` (422 `pins_incomplete` with no laya config; pins 1/1/1; first row unchanged after policy v2), `a_generated_draft_cannot_transition_a_card` (refused L1 and accepted L1 are 422 `draft_requires_gate`; the human `draft.apply` applies; `documents.update` attaching the generated class is 409 `draft_requires_gate`); `crates/actions/tests/ladder_human_gate.rs` — `a_service_principal_cannot_record_a_human_decision` (403 `person_required`), `a_human_decision_without_an_approved_human_gate_is_refused`, `a_pending_approval_cannot_gate_a_draft`, `only_a_human_draft_apply_decision_can_gate_a_draft`, `a_human_draft_apply_decision_and_approval_applies_the_draft`.
- **Action surface:** `ladder.record|evaluate|list|apply_draft`, `decision_policies.create|update|list`, `refinements.publish|list`, `laya_configs.create|list`; the human check is `human_approved_gate_tx`, the dedicated gate is `DRAFT_APPLY_GATE = "draft.apply"`, and every mutation appends `decision.changed`.
- **Governance:** tranche 2 (`01a1e9e0-e2ac-786b-ac48-3b8bcdf12188`) is `planned`, with no authorisation review, no `authorised_at` and no baseline reference; its exit criteria name S03 and T2. T2 closed on 2026-11-17 before that authorisation; the live register records the out-of-sequence closure as the accepted P0 issue `U3-EXC-T2` (`01a1fbac-aeb9-7dea-a079-bf159140344a`) under the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`.

## Verification

An independent reader can read the named test functions and run them against real Postgres 18 in the repository's harness: `crates/actions/tests/decision_ladder.rs` and `crates/actions/tests/ladder_human_gate.rs`. The compile/test verdict is the repository's GitHub-hosted `preflight.yml`; the local gate is `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1` (`docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md`). The rework records the acceptance instrument as `acceptance/programme/T2.toml`; it does not assert a manifest run the facts do not record.

## Links

- Issue: https://github.com/nonagenticai/conveyor/issues/73
- Commit: `39363ba8cfb532d415c9ad06b45e86421c5c86b6`
- Specification: `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §7.1–§7.5 and §12 (T2)
- Schema: `migrations/0046_decision_ladder.sql`
- Tests: `crates/actions/tests/decision_ladder.rs`, `crates/actions/tests/ladder_human_gate.rs`
- Tranche 2: `01a1e9e0-e2ac-786b-ac48-3b8bcdf12188`
- Standing delegation: `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`

## Gap

- **v1-t2-1 (P0, blocks closure).** A generated draft can be attached by `documents.compose`: the action accepts `card_id` and `meta.generated = true` and creates an attached document with no `draft.apply` check; `ladder.apply_draft` and the `documents.update` refusal do not cover the create path.
- **v1-t2-2.** L1 never calls laya: the answer, confidence, probabilities and latency are caller-supplied; no T2 path issues `POST /v1/systemone`.
